event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: VICI’s 2024 filing contains only one explicit reference to pandemic-type hazards. The company folds “public health crises” into a list of uncontrollable macro-factors that could hurt the gaming industry, alongside labor shortages, travel restrictions, supply-chain disruptions and property closures. The language is forward-looking and generic—there is no discussion of COVID-19 by name, no quantified impact and no description of lessons learned from 2020–2023 shutdowns. Nevertheless, the sentence acknowledges that such crises can materially affect tenant performance, and therefore VICI’s rental revenue. Given that the filing date is almost four years after the WHO declared COVID-19 a pandemic, the Time Decay Principle places the event in the medium-term band; a mid-level severity score (≈5) is appropriate: the risk remains relevant but is already partially absorbed into ordinary business-planning assumptions.

evidence_list.snippet: Other factors over which we and our tenants have no control, including public health crises, labor shortages, travel restrictions, supply chain disruptions and property closures, may also adversely affect the gaming industry.

components.reason: Explicitly flags ‘public health crises’—the core pandemic risk—as an uncontrollable factor.
Links the risk to the company’s revenue source by referencing potential adverse effects on ‘the gaming industry’.
Enumerates pandemic-related secondary impacts (labor shortages, travel restrictions, supply-chain disruptions, property closures).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: The sentence generically acknowledges multiple pandemic-style disruptions and ties them to the company’s sector, warranting a moderate score of 5 under medium-term Time Decay guidelines.
